request_state.literature: Literature (primary source arXiv:2412.11933, survey of solved cases): fully solved with all exponents>=3 are (3,3,n) for n<=10^9, (n,n,3) for n>=3, (n,n,n) for n>=3. Effective-finiteness only (not solved): (2p,2q,r) with p,q>=V_r [arXiv:2509.21083]. NOT solved: (4,4,5), (4,4,7), (4,6,3), any (2m,2n,r odd) with m!=n, (3,5,7), (5,5,7).
request_state.claim: Consolidated necessary conditions on any Beal counterexample, kernel-verified: the bases are pairwise coprime; A != B; the exponents are not all divisible by 3; x and y are not both divisible by 4 with z even; and neither 3 nor 4 divides gcd(x,y,z). Together with exponent reduction: if a counterexample exists, one exists with all exponents in {4} union {odd primes} AND satisfying all of these.
